newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria chancellor against bending EMU rules.
newsitem.headline: Austria chancellor against bending EMU rules.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky said on Thursday he opposed softening the Maastricht criteria for a single European currency even though Brussels has forecast Austria's accumulated debt may exceed the limit.
"I am against watering down the criteria just as I am against increasing their number," Vranitzky told a news conference during a one-day forum on the single currency.
"In the interest of the new currency's stability there can be no softening of the criteria," he continued.
The European Commission predicted earlier this month that Austria's debt to GDP ration would rise to 72.2 percent in 1997 from a projected 71.7 percent this year.
In order to qualify for European Economic and Monetary Union, member states should at least trim their debt towards the 60 percent of GDP ceiling laid down by Maastricht.
"Not only Austria is affected by the level of its debt. The critiria are open to interpretation and take into account tendency and dynamic," Vranitzky argued.
He added that Austria should easily fulfil all other criteria. -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
